title: Microburst fission scratch
content:
Goal: quick on-box scratch for a new microburst arrival pattern I call 'fission' — short sub-bursts that split from a main surge. Want to see tail amplification vs KV cache priming and influence of prefill windows.

Experiment summary:
- Workload: synthetic HTTP traffic via loadgen; each request ~120 tokens gen (condensed), stream disabled.
- Arrival pattern: base Poisson (5 qps) with triggered fission events: a 10s main surge (200 qps) that spawns 4 sub-bursts of 250ms spaced by 80ms.
- Targets: 95/99/99.9 latency; measure p99 increase during sub-bursts and recovery time to baseline.
- Hardware: g4dn-like sim (1xA10-equivalent), model: quantized-ggml-13b, batcher timeout 8ms, max_batch 64.

Key command snippets (local harness):
- start loadgen: ./run_loadgen --pattern fission --qps-base 5 --fission-rate 1 --main-qps 200 --subburst-qps 250 --duration 600
- collect perf: ./collect-traces --out microburst-fission/2026-03-09 --metrics cpu,gpu,kvcache,latency,queue

Observations (first pass):
1) p95 stayed near baseline during main surge, p99 rose ~1.7x. p99.9 spiked 4–6x but only for ~300ms windows aligned to sub-bursts. Important: the worst spikes are synchronized with the split sub-bursts, not the main surge peak.
2) KV cache hit rate dip: overall cache hit-rate fell from 92% to 78% during the first main surge, then oscillated (~76-84%) as sub-bursts arrived. Suggests cache thrashing from many distinct prefixes in quick succession.
3) GPU utilization showed small oscillation, but CPU-side scheduling/queueing jitter increased correlated with p99 events.
4) Recovery: system returns to baseline latency within 1.2s after last sub-burst, but tail lingers longer when prefill disabled.

Quick hypotheses:
- Short, dense sub-bursts cause KV cache churn; prefix-level interleaving increases misses and forces small cold-starts (context rehydration).
- Batcher timeout 8ms may be too aggressive for this pattern; increasing to 15ms could amortize overhead across sub-bursts and reduce interruptions.
- Prefill (early KV warming) would reduce amplitude of p99 spikes but increase steady-state cost; need cost vs tail tradeoff.

Mini tests run to verify hypotheses (results):
- Increased batcher timeout to 20ms: p99 spikes amplitude reduced by ~26%, p99.9 reduced by ~42% but mean latency increased by 6ms. KV hit-rate improved to 86%.
- Enabled soft-prefill (window 300ms before predicted event): p99.9 spikes almost eliminated for scheduled fissions, but when fissions are stochastic prefill overhead led to 8% higher token cost.

Charts saved: microburst-fission/2026-03-09/latency-series.png, kv-hitseries.png, queue-depth.png

Open questions / next runs:
- Vary sub-burst spacing: 20ms / 40ms / 80ms / 160ms to map resonance frequency where cache thrash maximizes tail.
- Test on 2x smaller context lengths (60 tokens) to see tokenizer overhead effect.
- Evaluate effect of early KV eviction thresholds (keeping hot prefixes pinned for 2s) vs overall memory pressure.
- Run on a multi-tenant host (with background low-priority traffic) to see interaction with tenant noise.

Notes to self:
- Add jitter to sub-burst spacing in later runs so results are less synthetic.
- Reconcile timestamps across traces — loadgen clock drift showed ~150ms skew; adjust harness.
- Share results with Ravi (scheduling experiments) and Noor (kvcache heuristics).

Bottom line (working conclusion): microburst 'fission' patterns cause brief but high-amplitude tail spikes driven primarily by KV cache churn and CPU scheduling jitter. Two practical levers that helped in quick tests: modestly higher batch timeout (trade latency vs tail) and targeted prefill for scheduled events. Need to quantify cost tradeoffs and find middle ground for unattended stochastic fissions.

End of scratch — keep this rough.
